metadata.title: Instant Photo Book Platform Data Assets
metadata.description: Catalog of the customer, identity and consent, photo and curation, book project and design, commerce and order, production and fulfilment, and support, growth and content data assets that power PastBook's one-click photo book platform: photos with EXIF timestamps, locations and the faces of children imported over encrypted connections from the phone camera roll, Facebook (albums, timeline, captions, years 2009–2025), computer, Dropbox and Google Drive; curation results produced in under 60 seconds; book projects, catalogue and price lists in seven currencies; tokenised card and PayPal payments; orders, print files and shipments routed to partner facilities on four continents and 150+ delivery countries; 24/7 support tickets and reprints; campaigns, attribution and lifecycle messages in ten languages; Trustpilot and App Store reviews. Governance covers GDPR (Dutch company, EU customers), CCPA (about 80% of customers in the US), Meta Platform Terms, PCI DSS scope kept at the payment providers, the care owed to children's images, consumer law on returns and reprints, FSC chain-of-custody, short retention of photos and print files after delivery, EU residency with regional CDN and partner copies, backing stores and team ownership.

rootGroups.name: Customer, Identity and Consent Data
rootGroups.description: The data that says who a PastBook customer is, how they sign in, what they have allowed PastBook to do with their photos and what the platform did on their behalf: the customer account behind the 10+ million books created since 2012, the login and social-login identity used across the iOS and Android app (1M+ downloads) and pastbook.com, the consent records that carry GDPR (Dutch company, EU customers) and CCPA (about 80% of customers in the United States) rights and Meta Platform Terms obligations, the append-only audit trail and the pseudonymous analytics events that measure the promise of a book in under 60 seconds. Access is concentrated on the customer themselves, the support agents who help them and the platform team that runs identity and privacy tooling.

subGroups.name: Accounts and Identity
subGroups.description: The customer account as the anchor for orders, books and reminders, and the user identity that authenticates customers with e-mail, Apple, Google or Facebook Login across app and web.

assets.name: Customer Account
assets.description: One consumer relationship with PastBook: display name, e-mail address, preferred language (one of ten site languages) and currency (USD, EUR, GBP, CAD, AUD, NZD, BRL), country, saved shipping addresses, marketing and push preferences, the linked book projects and the order history (Year in Review books, calendars, posters, gift cards), yearbook reminder settings and the account status (active, deletion requested, deleted). Created when a customer first previews a book or checks out as a guest in the Mobile App Shell (mapp) or web creator and mastered by Customer Account and Order History (acct), with Identity and Social Login (iden) holding the credentials separately. Lifecycle Messaging and Yearbook Reminders (lcyc) reads the language, country and last-order data to time reminders for the next yearbook, calendar or holiday gift. About 80% of accounts belong to US customers, then Australia, Europe and the UK, so the record is dual-regulated under CCPA and GDPR.
assets.businessMeaning: The record that ties a person to their books, orders, reprints and reminders: if it is wrong, the wrong address receives a book, the wrong currency is charged and the wrong language is spoken on WhatsApp.
assets.accessScope: the customer for their own account; support agents on WhatsApp, e-mail and chat for order changes and address fixes after identity verification; growth marketers only in pseudonymised segments; never visible to print partners beyond the shipping address on a job

interfaces.name: customer-account api
interfaces.description: Account creation, profile, language and currency, saved addresses, reminder and marketing preferences, order-history lookup and deletion-request API used by the app shell, the web creator, checkout, the support desk and lifecycle messaging.

interfaces.name: customer account events
interfaces.description: Account created, address added, preferences changed, first order placed, yearbook reminder scheduled, deletion requested and account erased events consumed by lifecycle messaging, the support desk, analytics and the audit trail.

governance.retention: kept while the account is active and 24 months after the last order or sign-in, then anonymised; erased within 30 days of a GDPR or CCPA deletion request except the order and payment records the Dutch fiscal retention duty requires for 7 years
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to PastBook; name, e-mail and address shared with the marketing/CRM platform and support desk vendors as processors; only the shipping name and address travel to print partners and carriers on a job; never sold, which also satisfies the CCPA 'do not sell' expectation

assets.name: User Identity
assets.description: A login to the PastBook app or pastbook.com: e-mail and password hash or a social identity from Sign in with Apple, Google or Facebook Login, device registrations and push tokens for iOS and Android, sessions and refresh tokens, roles for staff users (support agent, growth marketer, operations manager, administrator) and the link to the customer account. Managed by Identity and Social Login (iden), which also keeps the Facebook user id needed to honour Meta's data-deletion callback when a customer removes the PastBook app from their Facebook settings. Staff identities carry the 24/7 shift roles used by the support desk in the Netherlands, United States, Sri Lanka and India.
assets.businessMeaning: The gate to a person's private photos, books and payment history: a wrong role lets an agent see a stranger's children; a lost Facebook user id means a deletion callback cannot be honoured.
assets.accessScope: the user for their own profile and devices; platform administrators for role management; support agents for password-reset assistance without credential visibility; credentials, refresh tokens and social-login secrets never readable by anyone

interfaces.name: identity api
interfaces.description: Authentication, social login (Apple, Google, Facebook), session and refresh tokens, device and push-token registration, staff role checks, password reset and Meta deletion-callback handling used by every app and web module.

interfaces.name: identity events
interfaces.description: User registered, social identity linked, device registered, staff role granted or revoked, suspicious sign-in and identity deleted events consumed by the audit trail, analytics, lifecycle messaging and the support desk.

governance.retention: kept while the account exists; sessions expire per policy, sign-in logs 12 months, push tokens deleted when the device unregisters; the Facebook user id kept only as long as the connection exists so Meta deletion callbacks can be matched
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to PastBook; push tokens shared with Apple and Google for delivery only; social identifiers never shared with any other party

subGroups.name: Consent, Audit and Analytics
subGroups.description: The consent records that make photo import lawful, the append-only audit trail that proves who accessed which photos and orders, and the pseudonymous analytics events behind conversion and experimentation.

assets.name: Consent Record
assets.description: A dated, versioned record of what a customer agreed to: the privacy statement and terms version, the photo-library permission granted on iOS or Android, the Facebook Login permission scope Meta allowed (user_photos, albums, timeline pictures, cover and profile photos, mobile uploads, years 2009–2025), Dropbox and Google Drive OAuth scopes, marketing e-mail and push consent, cookie and tracking choices (including App Tracking Transparency), and the CCPA 'do not sell or share' opt-out. Facebook Connect and Year Selector (fbim) writes the Meta consent at connection time and Privacy, Consent and Data Deletion (priv) is the system of record that also holds withdrawal and deletion requests. Because photos routinely show children, consent to process the images is recorded per source and per import, not just once at signup.
assets.businessMeaning: The legal basis for touching a person's photos at all: without a valid record the import, the curation and the book are unlawful, and Meta app review will fail.
assets.accessScope: the customer for their own consents; the platform and data team for deletion handling and Meta callbacks; support agents see consent status only; marketing sees only the aggregated opt-in counts

interfaces.name: consent api
interfaces.description: Record, read, version and withdraw consents per source and purpose, check marketing and tracking permission, register a Meta or App Store deletion request and report its status; used by import bricks, lifecycle messaging and the privacy tooling.

interfaces.name: consent events
interfaces.description: Consent granted, scope changed, consent withdrawn, deletion requested and deletion completed events consumed by import bricks, the marketing/CRM platform, analytics suppression and the audit trail.

governance.retention: kept for the life of the account and 3 years after withdrawal or deletion as proof of the lawful basis; Meta-related consent records deleted when Meta's deletion callback is fulfilled
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to PastBook; opt-in and opt-out status pushed to the marketing/CRM and analytics processors as suppression flags; deletion confirmations returned to Meta as required by the Platform Terms; never shared otherwise

assets.name: Audit Trail Entry
assets.description: An immutable, hash-chained record of a privileged or externally visible action: a support agent opening a customer's book or photos, a staff export, a photo deletion, a Meta Graph API, Dropbox or Google Drive call made with a customer's token, a payment provider request, a carrier label request, a print file being sent to or purged from a partner, a consent change or an account erasure. Written by Privacy, Consent and Data Deletion (priv) and by the Integration Gateway (intg) for every outbound call, with retention tiers per entry type. It is what PastBook produces for a GDPR access request, a Meta data-use audit or a PCI DSS evidence request.
assets.businessMeaning: The proof that private photos and payment data were only touched for the order the customer asked for; without it PastBook cannot answer a regulator, Meta or a worried parent.
assets.accessScope: the platform and data team and the privacy officer for investigations; the customer for a report of who accessed their own account and photos on request; append-only, no edit or delete rights for anyone

interfaces.name: audit trail api
interfaces.description: Append entries, query by customer, staff user, partner or external system and time range, verify chain integrity and export a per-customer access report; used by privacy tooling, security monitoring and support escalations.

interfaces.name: audit events
interfaces.description: Privileged access, external call, export, deletion and consent-change events streamed to security monitoring and the analytics warehouse in pseudonymised form.

governance.retention: access and external-call entries kept 24 months, deletion and consent entries 7 years, payment-related entries per PCI DSS evidence needs; entries are never edited, only expired by tier
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to PastBook; extracts provided to the customer for their own access report, to Meta or a payment provider on audit request and to a supervisory authority on lawful request

assets.name: Analytics Event
assets.description: A pseudonymous product event from the app or web: app opened, photo source chosen (camera roll by date, location, album or Yearbook mode; Facebook year; computer, Dropbox or Google Drive), import started and completed with photo counts, curation finished with seconds elapsed, preview shown, edit actions, format and cover chosen, promo applied, checkout started and order placed, plus experiment assignments and crash and performance metrics. Emitted by the Mobile App Shell (mapp) and every web module and collected by Analytics and Experimentation (anly), keyed by a rotating pseudonymous id rather than the customer id. Events feed the 'minutes from opening the app to ordering a book' north star and the funnel from install to preview to paid order.
assets.businessMeaning: The instrument panel for the 60-second promise and preview-to-order conversion; the only data on which growth experiments and curation improvements can be judged.
assets.accessScope: product, curation and growth teams in aggregated dashboards; the platform and data team for pipeline diagnostics; individual event streams re-identifiable only by the platform team for support debugging with the customer's consent

interfaces.name: analytics api
interfaces.description: Event ingestion with consent-aware suppression, experiment assignment lookup, funnel and cohort queries and dashboard feeds used by the app shell, the web creator, the growth console and the curation team.

interfaces.name: analytics event stream
interfaces.description: Batched pseudonymous product events flowing from clients through the gateway into the warehouse and to the attribution engine.

governance.retention: raw events kept 13 months so two holiday seasons can be compared, aggregated metrics indefinitely; events of customers who opt out of tracking are not collected and existing events are purged on account erasure
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to PastBook; aggregated conversion data shared with the attribution/MMP partner and ad platforms only as consented and hashed; never shared with print partners

rootGroups.name: Photos and Curation Data
rootGroups.description: The most sensitive data PastBook holds and the raw material of every book: the photos themselves, imported over encrypted connections from the phone camera roll, from Facebook (albums, cover and profile photos, timeline pictures and mobile uploads, one year at a time from 2009 to 2025), from a computer, Dropbox or Google Drive, with EXIF timestamps, locations and the faces of family members and children; the OAuth tokens that make those imports possible under the Meta Platform Terms and the Dropbox and Google APIs; and the outputs of the intelligent curation engine that in under 60 seconds scores quality, removes duplicates and blurry shots, groups photos into moments and picks the best ones. Retention is deliberately short: photos exist to make one book, not to build an archive.

subGroups.name: Photo Assets and Sources
subGroups.description: The imported photo files and their metadata, and the connections to the phone library, Facebook, Dropbox and Google Drive through which they arrive.

assets.name: Photo Asset
assets.description: One imported photograph and its metadata: the original file (JPEG or HEIC) and generated thumbnails and print-resolution renditions, EXIF capture timestamp, camera and GPS location where present, pixel dimensions and orientation, the source (camera roll by date, location, album or Yearbook mode; Facebook album, timeline, cover or profile photo with its caption and posting date; computer upload; Dropbox or Google Drive path), the import batch and the customer and book projects it belongs to. Uploaded over encrypted connections by Photo Library Access and Import (phot), Upload from Computer, Dropbox and Google Drive (upld) and Facebook Connect and Year Selector (fbim), stored and served by Photo Media Storage and CDN (medi) and read by every curation brick. A typical family yearbook import brings thousands of photos in which children, partners and friends are recognisable, so the asset is treated as sensitive personal data regardless of the customer's own age.
assets.businessMeaning: The customer's memories in PastBook's custody: the whole business is the trust that these photos are used for one book, kept briefly and never seen by anyone else.
assets.accessScope: the customer for their own photos; curation services and the renderer by system identity only; support agents see thumbnails of a book only after the customer asks for help with that book and the access is audited; never browsable by staff, marketing or print partners outside the rendered print file

interfaces.name: photo media api
interfaces.description: Encrypted upload with resumable chunks, signed short-lived read URLs for thumbnails and print renditions via the CDN, metadata lookup by import batch or book project and per-photo or per-account deletion used by the import, editing, curation and rendering bricks.

interfaces.name: photo asset events
interfaces.description: Import batch started and completed with counts, photo stored, renditions generated, photo removed from a project and photos purged events consumed by curation, the book project, analytics (counts only) and the audit trail.

interfaces.name: original photo files
interfaces.description: Customer originals and generated renditions held as objects in encrypted photo storage and served through signed CDN URLs; never exposed as public links.

governance.retention: photos of an unfinished project deleted 90 days after the last activity; photos of an ordered book kept until 30 days after delivery so a reprint can be produced, then purged; Facebook-sourced photos deleted on Meta deletion callback or connection removal, whichever comes first; immediate erasure on customer request
governance.residency: eu; CDN edge caches in the customer's region with short TTLs
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to PastBook; only the rendered print file, not the photos, goes to a print partner; never shared with Meta, advertisers or any other party; never used to train models without explicit opt-in

assets.name: Photo Source Connection
assets.description: The link between a customer and a photo source: the iOS or Android photo-library permission state and last sync cursor for Photo Library Access and Import (phot); the Facebook Login connection with the Meta user id, granted permission scope, the available years 2009–2025 with album and photo counts and the long-lived token reference; and the Dropbox or Google Drive OAuth connection with folder scope and refresh-token reference for Upload from Computer, Dropbox and Google Drive (upld). Facebook Connect and Year Selector (fbim) is the system of record for the Facebook connection, the Integration Gateway (intg) performs every Graph API, Dropbox and Google Drive call with the token and the secret material itself lives only in the token vault. The record also carries the Instagram connections that were retired when Instagram discontinued third-party access for personal accounts.
assets.businessMeaning: The key to a person's entire photo history on another platform: a leaked token exposes years of private photos, and a misused one breaks Meta Platform Terms and PastBook's app review status.
assets.accessScope: the customer for their own connections; the Integration Gateway by system identity for API calls; the web creator and platform teams for sync diagnostics without token visibility; tokens readable by the gateway alone

interfaces.name: photo source connection api
interfaces.description: Connect a source, refresh and revoke tokens, list Facebook years and albums or cloud folders with counts, track sync cursors and import progress and disconnect a source with data purge; used by the import bricks, the gateway and privacy tooling.

interfaces.name: source connection events
interfaces.description: Source connected, scope granted, token refreshed or revoked, import synced, Meta deletion callback received and source disconnected events consumed by the import bricks, consent, audit and analytics.

governance.retention: kept while the connection is active; tokens revoked and the record deleted when the customer disconnects, removes the PastBook app in Facebook, Dropbox or Google settings or deletes the account; retired Instagram connections purged
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to PastBook; tokens used only against Meta Graph API, Dropbox and Google Drive on the customer's behalf; never shared with any other party

subGroups.name: Curation Results
subGroups.description: What the curation engine derives from a photo set in under 60 seconds: quality scores, duplicate and moment clusters and the ranked selection that becomes the book.

assets.name: Photo Quality Score
assets.description: Per-photo technical and aesthetic scores produced by Image Quality Scoring (qual): blur and focus, exposure and contrast, noise, resolution against the print size (a 12" × 8.5" large hardcover needs more pixels than an 8.5" × 6" small one), face count and face quality (eyes open, not cut off), composition and an overall printability score with the model version that produced it. Best-photo Selection and Ranking (sele) combines the scores with cluster context to decide what goes into the book. Scores are computed on renditions, stored without the pixels and are meaningless without the photo asset they belong to.
assets.businessMeaning: The reason a blurry or badly exposed shot never reaches the printed page: it drives photo selection acceptance and, downstream, print-quality complaints and reprints.
assets.accessScope: curation services by system identity; the curation AI team for model evaluation on pseudonymised or consented samples; never shown raw to customers, only as the resulting selection

interfaces.name: quality score api
interfaces.description: Score a batch of photos for a target product size, fetch scores by photo or import batch and report model version and latency; used by the selection ranker, the editor (warning on low-resolution swaps) and preflight.

interfaces.name: quality scoring events
interfaces.description: Batch scored, low-printability warnings and model version rolled out events consumed by selection, layout and analytics.

governance.retention: kept as long as the photo asset it scores and deleted with it; aggregated model-evaluation metrics kept without identifiers
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to PastBook; never shared externally; face-quality signals never used for identification

assets.name: Photo Cluster
assets.description: A grouping of photos within one import: near-duplicate clusters found by Duplicate and Near-duplicate Detection (dedu) through perceptual hashing and burst detection, and moment or event clusters built by Moment and Event Grouping (mmnt) from EXIF timestamps, GPS locations, Facebook posting dates and album membership and recurring faces, with a suggested moment title (for example a place and date) and time span. For a Facebook year the clusters follow the timeline of 2009–2025 posts; for a camera roll in Yearbook mode they follow the months of the year. Best-photo Selection and Ranking (sele) picks representatives per cluster so a book shows the day, not thirty shots of the same cake.
assets.businessMeaning: The structure that turns thousands of photos into a story of moments; wrong clusters mean duplicate pages or a birthday split across chapters.
assets.accessScope: curation services by system identity; the customer indirectly as the moments shown in the book preview and editor; the curation AI team on pseudonymised samples for grouping-quality review

interfaces.name: photo cluster api
interfaces.description: Create and query duplicate and moment clusters for an import, fetch a cluster's members and representative, rename or merge moments from the editor and report clustering latency; used by selection, layout and the editor.

interfaces.name: clustering events
interfaces.description: Duplicates detected, moments grouped and moment renamed events consumed by selection, layout and analytics (counts and seconds only).

governance.retention: kept as long as the photo assets of the import; any face grouping vectors deleted with the photos and never retained across projects
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to PastBook; never shared externally

assets.name: Selection Result
assets.description: The ranked outcome of curation for one book project: which photos Best-photo Selection and Ranking (sele) chose and why (quality score, cluster representative, chronological coverage, face presence), which were dropped as duplicates or blurry, the target page count derived from the product (24-page base, up to 300 pages hardcover, above 300 softcover), the ordering by moment and the customer's later overrides when they swap or remove photos in the editor. Smart Layout Generator (layo) consumes the selection to place photos on pages. The result is versioned so a customer's edits and the engine's automatic choice can be compared, which is how photo selection acceptance is measured.
assets.businessMeaning: The 'trust the automatic selection' promise made concrete: the acceptance rate of this result decides whether customers edit for an hour or order in a minute.
assets.accessScope: the customer through the preview and editor of their own book; curation services by system identity; the curation AI team for acceptance analysis on pseudonymised data

interfaces.name: selection api
interfaces.description: Run selection for a project and target product, fetch the current and original selection, record customer overrides and expose acceptance statistics; used by layout, the editor, the instant preview and analytics.

interfaces.name: selection events
interfaces.description: Selection completed with seconds elapsed and photo counts, photo overridden by customer and selection re-run events consumed by layout, the book project and analytics.

governance.retention: kept with the book project it belongs to and deleted with it; acceptance statistics retained without identifiers
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to PastBook; never shared externally

rootGroups.name: Book Projects and Design Data
rootGroups.description: The book as the customer sees it before it is an order: the book project that holds pages, cover, theme and captions for a photo book, wall calendar or poster, the shareable highlight video generated from it, the automatically generated page layouts and the theme and colour palettes that give a PastBook its look. Projects are created in the app and on pastbook.com in under a minute, previewed for free, edited by some customers and ordered by a fraction, so this data is high-volume, short-lived and personal because every page shows the customer's photos and captions.

subGroups.name: Book Projects and Preview
subGroups.description: The customer's project and the highlight video used to share it before ordering.

assets.name: Book Project
assets.description: One photo product in the making: the product type and size (Small Hardcover 8.5" × 6", Large Hardcover 12" × 8.5", wall calendar 8" × 11.7" or 11.7" × 16", folded or rolled poster 16.5" × 23.4"), the source it was built from (camera roll period or album, Facebook year 2009–2025, computer, Dropbox or Google Drive), the ordered pages with their layouts and photo placements, the cover photo, title and subtitle, theme colours, captions, dates and an optional quote and back-cover photo, the page count and resulting cover rule (up to 16 pages softcover, 18–26 choice, 27–300 hardcover, above 300 softcover), the project status (generating, previewed, edited, ordered, expired) and the version history. Created by the Web Book Creator (webc) or the mobile flow, edited by Page and Photo Editor (edit) and Cover, Theme and Add-on Designer (cvrd), shown by Instant Preview and Highlight Video Sharing (prev) and rendered to print by Print-ready PDF Rendering and Imposition (rndr). Facebook-sourced projects carry the original post captions and dates on each page.
assets.businessMeaning: The thing the customer decides to buy: its completeness in under 60 seconds drives preview-to-order conversion, and its exact content is what the printer must reproduce.
assets.accessScope: the customer for their own projects; support agents for a project the customer asks about, audited; the renderer by system identity once an order is paid; never browsable by other staff or partners

interfaces.name: book project api
interfaces.description: Create a project from a source and selection, read and update pages, cover, theme, captions and add-ons, change product size with page-count and cover-rule recalculation, version and restore, and lock the project at checkout; used by the app, the web creator, the editor, preview, cart and rendering.

interfaces.name: book project events
interfaces.description: Project generated with seconds elapsed, previewed, edited, size changed, locked for order and expired events consumed by analytics, lifecycle messaging (abandoned-preview reminders), checkout and rendering.

governance.retention: unordered projects expire and are deleted 90 days after the last activity with a reminder before; ordered projects kept 12 months so the customer can reorder or gift copies of past years, then reduced to the print file's lifetime; erased on account deletion
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to PastBook; only the rendered print file derived from it is shared with a print partner; a shareable preview link exposes the highlight video, not the editable project

assets.name: Preview Video
assets.description: The highlight video generated from a book project's selected photos and theme, introduced on iOS in July 2023 for sharing to family and social media before or after ordering: the rendered MP4 in social formats, the music track licence reference, the share link with expiry and view counts, and the photos and captions it includes. Produced and served by Instant Preview and Highlight Video Sharing (prev) through the media CDN. Because a share link can reach people who are not PastBook customers, links are unguessable, time-limited and revocable by the customer.
assets.businessMeaning: A viral loop for a private product: every shared highlight video is an advertisement the customer chose to make, and every link is a potential leak if handled badly.
assets.accessScope: the customer and anyone holding an unexpired share link; the mobile app team for rendering diagnostics without content; never indexed or listed publicly

interfaces.name: preview video api
interfaces.description: Generate a highlight video for a project, fetch signed playback URLs, create, expire and revoke share links and read share and view statistics; used by the mobile app, the web creator and analytics.

interfaces.name: preview video events
interfaces.description: Video generated, shared, viewed and link revoked events consumed by analytics and lifecycle messaging.

governance.retention: kept while the book project exists; share links expire after 30 days by default; deleted with the project or on request
governance.residency: eu; CDN edge caches in the viewer's region with short TTLs
governance.sharingPolicy: shared only through links the customer creates; never posted by PastBook; never shared with partners

subGroups.name: Layouts and Themes
subGroups.description: The design system of the automatic book: generated page layouts and the theme and colour palettes customers can switch between.

assets.name: Page Layout
assets.description: The generated design of one page or spread: the layout template chosen from the library, the photo slots with crop and placement of each selected photo, caption and date boxes with their text, the moment heading and the rules that applied (portrait versus landscape, faces kept out of the gutter, print bleed and safe zones for the chosen size), plus the customer's manual changes from the editor. Produced by Smart Layout Generator (layo) for the whole book in a single pass and edited slot by slot by Page and Photo Editor (edit). Layouts are stored as structured data, not images, so the same book can be re-rendered for a different size or a reprint.
assets.businessMeaning: The craft of the 'no design needed' promise: layouts decide whether faces are cut at the fold and whether a customer has to fix anything before ordering.
assets.accessScope: the customer through the preview and editor of their own book; curation and rendering services by system identity; the curation AI team for layout-quality analysis on pseudonymised data

interfaces.name: page layout api
interfaces.description: Generate layouts for a selection and product size, fetch and update slot placements, crops and captions, re-flow after a page or size change and expose layout templates; used by the editor, preview and rendering.

interfaces.name: layout events
interfaces.description: Layouts generated, page edited, re-flowed and template usage events consumed by the book project, analytics and the curation team.

governance.retention: kept with the book project and deleted with it; template usage statistics retained without identifiers
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to PastBook; expressed in the print file sent to a partner but never shared as data

assets.name: Design Theme
assets.description: A named theme in the PastBook catalogue of looks: colour palette for cover and backgrounds, typography for titles, captions and dates, cover styles and layout template family, seasonal and campaign themes (for example Year in Review), availability per product type and per language, and the default theme rules the engine applies from the photos' dominant colours. Mastered by Theme and Colour Palette Engine (thme), applied by Smart Layout Generator (layo) and offered to the customer in Cover, Theme and Add-on Designer (cvrd). Themes contain no customer data; their assignment to a project does.
assets.businessMeaning: The brand on every page: a small, well-maintained catalogue that keeps the automatic book looking designed and lets marketing launch a seasonal look without engineering.
assets.accessScope: all product, design and marketing staff read; the curation AI team and brand content team author and publish; customers see the published themes in the designer

interfaces.name: design theme api
interfaces.description: List, read and publish themes with palettes, typography and template families per product type and language, and resolve the default theme for a photo set; used by the layout generator, the designer and campaign management.

interfaces.name: theme events
interfaces.description: Theme published, retired and seasonal theme activated events consumed by the designer, layout and campaigns.

governance.retention: kept indefinitely as catalogue content; retired themes archived so past books can be re-rendered for reprints
governance.sharingPolicy: internal catalogue; published themes visible to all customers; not shared with partners

rootGroups.name: Commerce and Orders Data
rootGroups.description: The data that turns a previewed book into revenue: the product catalogue of books, calendars, posters and gift cards, price lists in seven currencies with page rules and extra-page prices, promotion codes and gift cards that run continuously and peak in Q4, the checkout session, the tokenised card and PayPal payment and the order itself with its per-country delivery promise. PastBook keeps the margin between the retail price and the partner print and shipping cost, so this data carries both the consumer-law obligations towards customers in 150+ countries and the PCI DSS scope that PastBook keeps as small as possible by never touching raw card numbers.

subGroups.name: Catalog, Pricing and Promotions
subGroups.description: What can be bought, at what price in which currency, and the discounts and gift cards that move demand.

assets.name: Product Catalog Item
assets.description: One sellable product configuration: Small Hardcover photo book 8.5" × 6" and Large Hardcover 12" × 8.5" with their 24-page base and page range up to 300 pages hardcover (softcover below 18 and above 300, choice between 18 and 26 pages), wall calendars 8" × 11.7" and 11.7" × 16" (iOS app), folded and rolled posters 16.5" × 23.4" (frame not included), gift cards, and add-ons such as the hardcover upgrade and back-cover photo; each with paper and finish specification, FSC-certified paper requirement, production specification identifier used by print partners, availability per country and channel (app, web, Facebook flow) and lifecycle status. Mastered by Product Catalog (ctlg) and priced by Pricing, Page Rules and Currencies (pric). Older releases quoted books up to 500 pages, so the catalogue keeps retired configurations for reprints of past orders.
assets.businessMeaning: The definition of what PastBook sells and what a partner must be able to produce; a mismatch between catalogue and partner specification is a rejected print job.
assets.accessScope: all staff read; the commerce team authors and publishes; production operations maintains the production specification per partner; customers see the published catalogue in the app and on pastbook.com

interfaces.name: product catalog api
interfaces.description: List and read products, sizes, page ranges, cover rules, add-ons, specifications and availability per country and channel, and publish or retire configurations; used by pricing, the book project, cart, rendering, partner routing and campaigns.

interfaces.name: catalog events
interfaces.description: Product published, specification changed, availability changed and product retired events consumed by pricing, routing, partner integration and localisation.

governance.retention: kept indefinitely; retired configurations archived while any order using them is within the reprint window or the fiscal retention period
governance.sharingPolicy: published to customers; production specifications shared with contracted print partners; not otherwise shared

assets.name: Price List
assets.description: The effective prices per product, currency and country as published on the pricing-and-shipping page: the 24-page Small Hardcover at USD 19.99 / EUR 24.99 / GBP 16.99 / CAD 29.99 / AUD 35.99 / NZD 41.99 / BRL 144.99 and the Large Hardcover at USD 34.99 / EUR 41.99 / GBP 27.99 / CAD 51.99 / AUD 62.99 / NZD 71.99 / BRL 252.99, extra pages at USD 0.40 (small) and USD 0.55 (large) each with their equivalents, the hardcover surcharge for 18–26-page books, calendar prices (USD 24.99 / EUR 29.99 and USD 34.99 / EUR 40.99), poster prices (folded USD 29.99 / EUR 34.99, rolled USD 39.99 / EUR 46.99), shipping prices per destination and tax treatment, each with validity dates and version. Mastered by Pricing, Page Rules and Currencies (pric) and applied by Cart and Checkout (cart); prices are the same for a book made from the phone, Facebook or the web. Historic versions are kept so any past order can be explained to a customer or an auditor.
assets.businessMeaning: The unit economics lever between retail price and partner cost: every page and every currency here decides gross margin, and a wrong price in one currency is a refund wave.
assets.accessScope: all staff read; the commerce team and finance author and approve price versions; growth marketing proposes campaign prices; customers see the published price for their country and currency

interfaces.name: price list api
interfaces.description: Resolve the price of a configured product for a country, currency and page count including extra pages, cover surcharge, shipping and tax, read published price lists and version history and publish new versions with validity; used by the book project, cart, checkout, campaigns and localisation of pricing pages.

interfaces.name: price list events
interfaces.description: Price version published and price changed per currency events consumed by the cart, the pricing pages, campaigns and analytics.

governance.retention: all versions kept for 7 years after their validity ends to explain historic orders under the Dutch fiscal retention duty
governance.sharingPolicy: published prices are public; cost-side data is internal to PastBook; not shared with partners

assets.name: Promotion Code
assets.description: A discount campaign artefact: the code or automatic promotion, its type (percentage, fixed amount, free shipping, free hardcover or size upgrade), eligible products, countries and currencies, validity window, usage limits per customer and in total, stacking rules, the marketing campaign it belongs to (Year in Review, Mother's Day, Black Friday and Christmas peaks, App Store featuring pushes) and redemption counts and discount value granted. Created in Campaign and Seasonal Promotion Management (camp) and validated and redeemed by Promotions, Discount Codes and Gift Cards (prom) at checkout. Promotions and discounts run continuously at PastBook, which is why the record tracks promo discipline: how much margin each code gave away per order.
assets.businessMeaning: The accelerator and the leak at once: promotions drive Q4 volume and install-to-order conversion, and undisciplined codes erode the margin per book.
assets.accessScope: growth marketers create and manage codes; the commerce team owns validation rules; support agents may apply a goodwill code to an order; redemption records visible per customer only to support and commerce

interfaces.name: promotion api
interfaces.description: Create and manage codes and automatic promotions with eligibility, validity and limits, validate and redeem at checkout, reverse on cancellation and report redemptions and discount value per campaign; used by campaigns, cart, checkout, the support desk and analytics.

interfaces.name: promotion events
interfaces.description: Promotion created, activated, redeemed, limit reached and expired events consumed by campaigns, checkout, lifecycle messaging and analytics.

governance.retention: codes and rules kept 3 years after expiry for campaign analysis; per-customer redemptions kept with the order for 7 years, anonymised on account erasure
governance.sharingPolicy: codes are public once published; redemption data internal to PastBook; aggregated performance shared with ad platforms only as conversion counts

assets.name: Gift Card
assets.description: A prepaid PastBook gift card bought by a Seasonal Gift Giver for parents, grandparents or a partner: the card code and value in one of the seven currencies, purchase order and payment reference, the recipient's name and e-mail and the delivery date of the digital card, the personal message, the balance and redemption history against orders, expiry per the consumer law of the customer's country and refund status. Issued and redeemed by Promotions, Discount Codes and Gift Cards (prom) at checkout. Outstanding balances are a liability in PastBook's books, so the record is reconciled with finance.
assets.businessMeaning: A gift for people who have no photos to print yet: the gift-card redemption rate measures whether gifting brings a second customer, and the unredeemed balance is money PastBook owes.
assets.accessScope: the buyer for their purchased cards and the recipient for their balance; support agents for balance questions and re-sends after verification; finance for liability reconciliation; card codes masked everywhere except at redemption

interfaces.name: gift card api
interfaces.description: Issue a card on payment, deliver or re-send the digital card, check balance, redeem partially or fully at checkout, reverse on refund and report outstanding liability; used by checkout, payments, the support desk and finance.

interfaces.name: gift card events
interfaces.description: Card issued, delivered, redeemed, balance exhausted, expired and refunded events consumed by orders, lifecycle messaging, the support desk and finance.

governance.retention: kept until 7 years after expiry or full redemption under the fiscal retention duty; recipient personal data minimised to name and e-mail and erased on request once the balance is used
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to PastBook; the recipient receives only the card and message; never shared with partners

subGroups.name: Checkout, Payments and Orders
subGroups.description: The purchase itself: the checkout session, the tokenised payment and the order that starts production.

assets.name: Checkout Session
assets.description: A customer's path from a finished book project to payment: the cart with one or more configured products (a book of a given size and page count, extra copies for family, a calendar, a poster), the resolved prices in the customer's currency, applied promotion codes and gift cards, shipping address and method with the quoted delivery window per country (US 4–8 business days after production, UK 4–5, France, Netherlands, Italy and Germany 3–5, rest of EU 5–7, Canada and Australia 5–10, New Zealand, India and Brazil 7–10), tax, the chosen payment method (Visa, Mastercard, American Express, PayPal) and the session state (open, abandoned, paid, expired). Managed by Cart and Checkout (cart) and handed to Payments (paym) for authorisation. Abandoned sessions drive the recovery reminders sent by lifecycle messaging.
assets.businessMeaning: The last 60 seconds of the funnel: where preview-to-order conversion is won or lost and where a wrong shipping window becomes a support ticket.
assets.accessScope: the customer for their own session; support agents for checkout problems after verification; the commerce team for funnel diagnostics on pseudonymised data; payment method details never stored here beyond type and last four digits

interfaces.name: checkout api
interfaces.description: Create and update a cart, add configured products and copies, apply promotions and gift cards, quote shipping options and delivery windows, compute totals with tax and start payment; used by the app, the web creator, payments and lifecycle messaging.

interfaces.name: checkout events
interfaces.description: Checkout started, item added, promotion applied, shipping chosen, abandoned, paid and expired events consumed by payments, orders, analytics and lifecycle messaging (abandoned-cart reminders).

governance.retention: abandoned sessions deleted after 30 days (after recovery reminders have run); paid sessions kept with the order; erased on account deletion
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to PastBook; address and totals passed to the payment provider for fraud screening; never shared otherwise

assets.name: Payment Transaction
assets.description: The money movement for an order or gift card: authorisation, capture, refund and chargeback records from the card acquirer (Visa, Mastercard, American Express) or PayPal, the provider's payment token and transaction reference, amount and currency out of the seven, fraud-screening result, 3-D Secure outcome, payment status and settlement and fee data for reconciliation. PastBook never stores card numbers: Payments (paym) uses provider-hosted fields and tokens, so PCI DSS scope is limited to the token and the Integration Gateway (intg) that calls the providers, and Order Management and Status (ordr) reads the status to start production. Refunds for reprint-or-refund cases and chargebacks are recorded against the original transaction.
assets.businessMeaning: Cash in and the trigger for production, which starts on payment: an authorisation that never captures is a book printed for free, and a chargeback trend is a fraud or quality signal.
assets.accessScope: the customer for their own receipts; finance for reconciliation and refunds; support agents for payment status and refund initiation after verification; card data never present, provider tokens readable by the payment service alone

interfaces.name: payment api
interfaces.description: Start and confirm a payment through provider-hosted fields or PayPal, capture, refund partially or fully, read status and receipt data and export settlement records; used by checkout, orders, reprint and refund handling, finance and the gateway.

interfaces.name: payment events
interfaces.description: Payment authorised, captured, failed, refunded, disputed and settled events consumed by orders, production job creation, the support desk, finance and analytics.

governance.retention: kept 7 years under the Dutch fiscal retention duty; provider tokens invalidated after the refund window; dispute evidence kept until the dispute closes
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with the card acquirer and PayPal as processors under PCI DSS; amounts and references shared with the accounting system; never shared with print partners or marketing

assets.name: Order
assets.description: A paid purchase: order number, customer, ordered lines (book with size, page count and cover type, copies, calendar, poster, gift card) each referencing the locked book project version, prices, discounts and gift-card redemption, tax and totals in the customer's currency, shipping address and method with the promised delivery window, the order status from paid through in production, shipped, delivered, cancelled or refunded, the linked production jobs and shipments, the packing slip content and any address changes made by support before production. Mastered by Order Management and Status (ordr), shown in Customer Account and Order History (acct) and read by Support Desk (sprt) on every contact. Multi-product orders ship together on the longest production time, and the 10+ million books created since 2012 live here as orders.
assets.businessMeaning: The contract with the customer and the unit of everything downstream: production, shipping, support, reprints, revenue and the on-time-delivery promise.
assets.accessScope: the customer for their own orders; support agents for order changes, tracking and reprints after verification; production operations for routing and status; finance for revenue; print partners see only the job derived from the order with the shipping address

interfaces.name: order api
interfaces.description: Create an order from a paid checkout, read order and line status, change address or cancel before production, link production jobs and shipments, record delivery and refunds and list order history per account; used by the account, support desk, reprint handling, routing, shipping, lifecycle messaging and finance.

interfaces.name: order events
interfaces.description: Order placed, address changed, cancelled, in production, shipped, delivered and refunded events consumed by production routing, shipping, the support desk, lifecycle messaging, analytics and finance.

interfaces.name: packing slip
interfaces.description: Per-order packing slip content generated for the print partner and included in the parcel.

governance.retention: kept 7 years under the Dutch fiscal retention duty; personal fields pseudonymised on account erasure while amounts and product lines remain for accounting
governance.sharingPolicy: job data and shipping address shared with the routed print partner and carrier; order totals with the accounting system; order status with the support desk and CRM processors; never sold

rootGroups.name: Production and Fulfilment Data
rootGroups.description: The data that gets a paid book printed and delivered by partner facilities on four continents, most of them in the customer's own country, to 150+ countries: the imposed print-ready PDF and its preflight report, the production job routed to the facility with capacity and lowest cost, the profiles and SLAs of the partners, the shipping rates and the tracked shipment against the published delivery windows, and the quality incidents that feed reprint root causes and partner audits. Print files contain the customer's photos, so they live in storage with a time-to-live and are purged from PastBook and from partners shortly after delivery; FSC chain-of-custody and local production are how the sustainability claims are evidenced.

subGroups.name: Print Preparation
subGroups.description: From locked book project to a production job: the print-ready file, its preflight verdict and the job that carries both to a partner.

assets.name: Print File
assets.description: The imposed, print-ready PDF set for one ordered product: cover file and block file for a Small or Large Hardcover or softcover book with bleed, spine width calculated from the page count, colour profile and the partner's specification, calendar or poster files, plus the packing slip and job ticket, with checksums, file sizes and the render engine version. Produced by Print-ready PDF Rendering and Imposition (rndr) from the locked book project after payment, stored by Photo Media Storage and CDN (medi) in a bucket with a time-to-live, checked by Preflight and Print Quality Checks (pflt) and pushed by Print Partner Integration (pint) to the facility's API or hot folder. It embeds every photo of the book at print resolution and therefore inherits the sensitivity of the photos and the customer's captions.
assets.businessMeaning: The handover artefact to a partner PastBook does not own: a wrong spine, profile or version is a defective book, a leaked file is the customer's family album in the open.
assets.accessScope: rendering, preflight and partner integration services by system identity; the routed print partner through a signed, expiring download or hot-folder transfer; production operations may open a file for a quality investigation, audited; never accessible to marketing or other partners

interfaces.name: print file api
interfaces.description: Render and impose files for an order line against a partner specification, fetch signed expiring download URLs, verify checksums, re-render for a reprint and purge files after delivery; used by preflight, partner integration, reprint handling and privacy tooling.

interfaces.name: print file events
interfaces.description: Render started, rendered, preflight passed or failed, delivered to partner and purged events consumed by routing, partner integration, quality monitoring and the audit trail.

interfaces.name: print-ready pdf set
interfaces.description: Cover and block PDFs, calendar or poster PDFs, job ticket and packing slip transferred to the routed partner facility by API or hot folder.

governance.retention: kept until 30 days after confirmed delivery so a reprint can be produced without re-rendering, then purged automatically by storage TTL; partners are contractually required to delete files within 30 days of shipping; erased earlier on customer request after the order has shipped
governance.residency: eu; a copy at the routed partner facility in the production country for the duration of production
governance.sharingPolicy: shared only with the single routed print partner under a data processing agreement; never shared with any other party

assets.name: Preflight Report
assets.description: The automated verdict on a print file before it leaves PastBook: page count and spine consistency with the order, bleed and safe-zone compliance, image resolution per placed photo against the print size (flagging low-resolution phone or Facebook photos that will look soft in print), colour profile and font embedding, file integrity, partner-specification match and the pass, warn or fail decision with the checks that failed. Produced by Preflight and Print Quality Checks (pflt) for every file and every re-render. A failing report blocks routing and opens a task for engineering or support, and warning rates per source (Facebook years from 2009 tend to be lower resolution) inform curation thresholds.
assets.businessMeaning: The gate between a paid order and a partner's press: its failure rate is the print file rejection rate partners are measured on, and its warnings predict print-quality complaints.
assets.accessScope: print and fulfilment engineering and production operations for diagnostics; support agents see the verdict on an order they handle; partners receive only the job ticket, not the report

interfaces.name: preflight api
interfaces.description: Run preflight on a print file for a partner specification, read the report and check results per file, override a warning with a reason and report rejection and warning rates per source, product and partner; used by routing, partner integration, reprint handling and quality monitoring.

interfaces.name: preflight events
interfaces.description: Preflight passed, passed with warnings, failed and override recorded events consumed by routing, quality monitoring and analytics.

governance.retention: kept 12 months for quality analysis, then aggregated without identifiers; deleted earlier with the order on account erasure
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to PastBook; rejection statistics shared with a partner about its own specification only

assets.name: Production Job
assets.description: One unit of work for a partner facility: the order line and copies to produce, product and specification, the routed partner and facility, the print file references, the routing decision and reasons (customer country, partner capacity and cutoff, unit cost, SLA, current backlog), the promised production time and ship-by date, status callbacks from the partner (received, in production, printed, bound, packed, handed to carrier, on hold, rejected) with timestamps, and the reprint flag when the job replaces a defective one. Created by Print Partner Routing (rout), exchanged through Print Partner Integration (pint) and watched by Production SLA and Quality Monitoring (qmon). Production starts on payment and multi-product orders are held so all jobs ship together on the longest production time.
assets.businessMeaning: The heartbeat of on-time production: routing quality here decides unit cost, delivery days and whether the holiday peak overwhelms a facility.
assets.accessScope: production operations and print and fulfilment engineering for the network; the routed partner for its own jobs through the partner API or portal; support agents for the status of an order they handle; never visible to other partners

interfaces.name: production job api
interfaces.description: Create and route jobs, re-route on rejection or capacity, read status and timeline, receive partner status callbacks, hold and release multi-product orders and report jobs per partner, status and SLA; used by partner integration, shipping, quality monitoring, the support desk and the control tower.

interfaces.name: production job events
interfaces.description: Job routed, sent to partner, accepted, in production, printed, packed, handed over, rejected, re-routed and reprint created events consumed by shipping, quality monitoring, orders, the support desk and analytics.

interfaces.name: partner job feed
interfaces.description: Job tickets and status files exchanged with partners that use a hot folder rather than the API.

governance.retention: kept 3 years for partner performance and cost analysis, then aggregated; personal fields pseudonymised on account erasure
governance.sharingPolicy: job details shared with the routed partner only; aggregated volumes shared with each partner for capacity planning

subGroups.name: Partner Network and Shipping
subGroups.description: The partners and carriers PastBook orchestrates, and the shipments and quality incidents that measure them.

assets.name: Print Partner Profile
assets.description: The record of a partner printing facility in the network on four continents (for example in the United States, the European Union, the United Kingdom, Australia, Brazil or India): company and facility details, contacts and escalation paths, supported products and specifications (hardcover and softcover books, calendars, posters), integration mode (order API or hot folder, status callbacks), daily capacity and holiday-peak commitments, order cutoff times, production SLA per product, unit cost and price list, carriers used, countries served, FSC certification and chain-of-custody status, sustainability commitments, data processing agreement and file-deletion terms, quality audit results and current status (active, limited, suspended). Maintained by production operations and used by Print Partner Routing (rout) to decide where each job goes and by Print Partner Integration (pint) to connect. Because most orders are produced in the customer's own country, the profile's country coverage and peak commitments are what make the Q4 season and the local-production sustainability claim feasible.
assets.businessMeaning: The configuration of a print utility PastBook does not own: capacity, cost and SLA per partner decide local production, shipping emissions, delivery days and margin.
assets.accessScope: production operations authors and maintains; print and fulfilment engineering for routing and integration configuration; finance for unit cost and settlement; each partner sees its own profile in the partner portal; commercial terms never visible to other partners

interfaces.name: print partner api
interfaces.description: Read and update partner facilities, specifications, capacity and cutoffs, SLAs, unit costs, integration credentials references, certification and status, and expose the eligible-partner set for a country and product; used by routing, partner integration, quality monitoring and the control tower.

interfaces.name: partner profile events
interfaces.description: Partner onboarded, capacity changed, cutoff changed, suspended or reactivated and audit recorded events consumed by routing and quality monitoring.

governance.retention: kept for the life of the partner relationship and 7 years after for contract and fiscal purposes; contact personal data minimised to business roles
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to PastBook; each partner sees only its own profile; certification status may be summarised publicly on the sustainability page

assets.name: Shipping Rate
assets.description: The shipping options and their prices and transit promises per origin facility and destination country: carrier and service level, price per product and copies in the seven currencies, the published transit windows after production (United States 4–8 business days, United Kingdom 4–5, France, Netherlands, Italy and Germany 3–5, rest of the EU 5–7, Canada and Australia 5–10, New Zealand, India and Brazil 7–10), holiday cutoff dates for delivery before Christmas or Mother's Day, free-shipping rules used as upgrade incentives, customs and duty treatment and the carrier contract behind each rate. Mastered by Shipping Rates, Carrier Labels and Tracking (ship) and quoted at checkout. Rates are versioned so a quoted window can be defended when a parcel is late.
assets.businessMeaning: The delivery promise made at checkout for 150+ countries: an optimistic window is a gift arriving after the occasion and a negative review within 48 hours.
assets.accessScope: all staff read; print and fulfilment engineering and production operations maintain rates and cutoffs; marketing reads holiday cutoffs for campaigns; customers see the options for their destination at checkout

interfaces.name: shipping rate api
interfaces.description: Quote shipping options, prices and delivery windows for a destination, product and origin facility, read holiday cutoffs and free-shipping rules and publish rate versions; used by checkout, the pricing pages, campaigns and label creation.

interfaces.name: shipping rate events
interfaces.description: Rate version published, carrier service changed and holiday cutoff set events consumed by checkout, the pricing pages and campaigns.

governance.retention: all versions kept 7 years so quoted windows and prices on historic orders can be explained
governance.sharingPolicy: published to customers; carrier contract terms internal to PastBook

assets.name: Shipment
assets.description: A parcel from a partner facility to the customer: the production jobs it contains, carrier and service, label and tracking number, recipient name and address, weight and dimensions, customs declaration where the parcel crosses a border, the ship date and promised delivery window, carrier tracking events from pickup to delivered or exception (address problem, customs hold, lost, returned), delivery confirmation and the delay flag against the promise. Created by Shipping Rates, Carrier Labels and Tracking (ship) when a partner marks a job packed, updated with carrier callbacks through the Integration Gateway (intg) and watched by Production SLA and Quality Monitoring (qmon). Tracking status is what customers ask about most on WhatsApp in December.
assets.businessMeaning: The last mile of the promise and the most-asked support question: on-time delivery rate in peak season is measured here, per country and per partner.
assets.accessScope: the customer for their own tracking; support agents for tracking questions and address issues after verification; production operations for carrier performance; the shipping partner and carrier for their own parcels

interfaces.name: shipment api
interfaces.description: Create labels and shipments for packed jobs, read tracking status and history, register carrier callbacks, flag exceptions and delays and report on-time delivery per country, carrier and partner; used by partner integration, the support desk, lifecycle messaging (shipping notifications), quality monitoring and the account.

interfaces.name: shipment events
interfaces.description: Shipment created, picked up, in transit, out for delivery, delivered, exception and delayed events consumed by the order, lifecycle messaging, the support desk, quality monitoring and analytics.

governance.retention: kept 3 years for carrier performance and claims; recipient address pseudonymised on account erasure once any claim window has closed
governance.sharingPolicy: recipient name and address shared with the carrier and, for customs, with authorities; tracking status shared with the customer through app, e-mail and support; never shared otherwise

assets.name: Quality Incident
assets.description: A recorded production or delivery failure: the affected order, job, partner and product, the incident type (print defect such as colour shift, banding or misaligned pages; binding or cover damage; wrong or missing pages; packaging damage; late production; lost or damaged parcel), evidence such as customer photos of the defect from the support conversation, the root cause once investigated (partner process, file or preflight gap, curation or low-resolution source, carrier), the corrective action, the cost of the reprint or refund and the SLA breach classification. Opened by Production SLA and Quality Monitoring (qmon) from partner callbacks and delays or by Reprint and Refund Handling (rprt) from a customer complaint, and reviewed with partners in quality audits. Incident rates per partner feed routing weights and the print defect rate KPI.
assets.businessMeaning: The feedback loop from a disappointed customer to a partner fix: reprint rate, defect rate and unit cost only move when incidents are recorded and attributed honestly.
assets.accessScope: production operations and print and fulfilment engineering for the network; support agents for incidents on orders they handle; each partner sees incidents attributed to its own facility; customer evidence photos visible only to support and quality staff

interfaces.name: quality incident api
interfaces.description: Open, classify, attribute and close incidents with evidence, root cause and corrective action, link to reprint cases and jobs and report defect, late and lost rates per partner, product and period; used by reprint handling, partner integration, routing and the control tower.

interfaces.name: quality incident events
interfaces.description: Incident opened, root cause set, partner notified, corrective action agreed and incident closed events consumed by routing weights, reprint handling, the support desk and analytics.

governance.retention: kept 3 years for partner performance and audits; customer evidence photos deleted 90 days after closure; personal fields pseudonymised on account erasure
governance.sharingPolicy: incident details shared with the attributed partner under the quality clauses of its contract; aggregated rates internal to PastBook

rootGroups.name: Support, Growth and Content Data
rootGroups.description: The data of PastBook's own operators around the product: the 24/7 support desk on WhatsApp, e-mail and chat staffed from the Netherlands, United States, Sri Lanka and India with its tickets, reprint cases and help articles; the growth engine of campaigns in ten languages and seven currencies with app-store and MMP attribution and lifecycle messages that bring customers back for the next yearbook; and the brand content of Trustpilot and App Store reviews (TrustScore 4.5 from 35,837 reviews, every negative review answered within 48 hours) and the localisation strings behind ten site languages. Much of it lives in SaaS tools acting as processors, so sharing and retention are governed through those vendors.

subGroups.name: Customer Care
subGroups.description: Tickets, reprint and refund cases and the help content that lets customers solve problems themselves.

assets.name: Support Ticket
assets.description: One customer contact and its conversation: channel (WhatsApp, e-mail, web or app chat), language, the customer and order or book project it concerns, the category (order change, address fix, tracking question, print-quality complaint, payment or promo issue, Facebook or import problem, privacy or deletion request, gift-card question), the transcript with attachments such as photos of a damaged book, the agent and shift location, priority, status, first response and resolution times and the customer satisfaction rating. Managed by Support Desk (sprt) in the support desk SaaS, which reads the order for context, and escalated to Reprint and Refund Handling (rprt) when a book has to be reprinted or refunded. Privacy and deletion requests arriving here are handed to the privacy tooling with the ticket kept as proof of handling.
assets.businessMeaning: The first-contact resolution promise in data: ticket volume per order and median first response time are the support north-star metrics, and the categories tell product and partners what breaks.
assets.accessScope: the customer for their own conversations; support agents and team leads across the four support locations; the brand team for anonymised review-response context; attachments with photos visible only to support and quality staff

interfaces.name: support ticket api
interfaces.description: Create tickets from WhatsApp, e-mail and chat, attach the customer, order and project context, update status, category and assignment, record satisfaction and export metrics; used by the support desk, reprint handling, the account (contact history) and analytics.

interfaces.name: support ticket events
interfaces.description: Ticket opened, first response sent, escalated to reprint, resolved, reopened and rated events consumed by reprint handling, quality monitoring, lifecycle messaging suppression and analytics.

governance.retention: kept 24 months after resolution for repeat-contact context and disputes, then anonymised; attachments with photos deleted 90 days after resolution; erased on account deletion unless a dispute is open
governance.residency: eu; support desk SaaS regions per vendor agreement
governance.sharingPolicy: processed by the support desk SaaS and WhatsApp Business as processors; order context shared with the print partner only when a reprint is needed; never shared otherwise

assets.name: Reprint Case
assets.description: The remedy for a failed book: the order and lines concerned, the customer's complaint and evidence, the decision (free reprint, reprint with correction, partial or full refund, goodwill discount), the linked quality incident and root cause, whether the customer edits the book before the reprint, the new production job routed to the same or a different partner, the shipping upgrade to still meet a gift date, refund transaction reference, the approver and the cost booked to PastBook or recovered from the partner. Managed by Reprint and Refund Handling (rprt) as the escalation path of the support desk, under the consumer-law expectation that a defective product is remedied without cost to the customer. Reprint rate per partner and per source is how quality is priced into routing.
assets.businessMeaning: The cost of quality made explicit: each case is margin lost on a book that should have been right the first time, and the fastest way to turn a one-star review into a five-star update.
assets.accessScope: support agents and team leads for handling and approval within limits; production operations for partner attribution and cost recovery; finance for refunds; the customer sees the outcome and tracking of the replacement

interfaces.name: reprint case api
interfaces.description: Open a case from a ticket, record decision and approval, trigger a reprint job with optional re-render and shipping upgrade or a refund, link the quality incident and cost attribution and report reprint and refund rates; used by the support desk, production routing, payments, quality monitoring and finance.

interfaces.name: reprint case events
interfaces.description: Case opened, approved, reprint job created, refund issued, cost attributed to partner and case closed events consumed by orders, routing, payments, quality monitoring and analytics.

governance.retention: kept 7 years where a refund or credit note is involved under the fiscal retention duty, otherwise 3 years for quality analysis; evidence photos deleted 90 days after closure
governance.sharingPolicy: the defect description and replacement job shared with the responsible partner; refund shared with the payment provider; never shared otherwise

assets.name: Help Article
assets.description: A published help-center article on help.pastbook.com and in the app: title, body, category (Photo Books, sizes and pages, pricing, shipping and delivery times, Facebook and photo sources, editing, payments, account and privacy), the ten language versions, related products, the FAQ snippets surfaced in chat and the search keywords, plus view counts, helpfulness votes and the tickets it deflected. Authored by the support team in Help Center and Self-service (help) and translated with the localisation strings. Articles state the operational facts customers ask about most, such as 'up to 16 pages softcover, 27–300 pages hardcover' and per-country delivery windows, so they must change the day a price or window changes.
assets.businessMeaning: Self-service that keeps the 24/7 desk small: a good article prevents hundreds of December tickets; an outdated one creates them.
assets.accessScope: public to read; the support team authors; the brand content team translates and reviews; the commerce and operations teams approve fact changes about prices and delivery

interfaces.name: help article api
interfaces.description: Create, translate, publish and retire articles, search articles and FAQ snippets per language and report views, votes and deflection; used by the help center, the in-app help, the chat bot and analytics.

interfaces.name: help article events
interfaces.description: Article published, updated, translated and retired events consumed by the help center, the chat bot and the localisation mirror.

governance.retention: kept indefinitely while published; retired versions archived 3 years for reference in disputes about what was promised
governance.residency: eu; help center SaaS regions per vendor agreement
governance.sharingPolicy: public content; no personal data

subGroups.name: Campaigns and Lifecycle
subGroups.description: The marketing calendar and its measurement, and the reminders that make a yearbook an annual habit.

assets.name: Marketing Campaign
assets.description: A planned and running growth activity: the campaign (Year in Review, Mother's Day, Black Friday and Christmas gifting, App Store featuring push, back-to-school yearbook), channels (paid social, paid search, App Store and Google Play ASO and featuring, e-mail, push, influencer and gift-guide placements such as GQ), target countries, languages out of ten and currencies out of seven, creative assets and messaging per language, budget and pacing by day with the Q4 peak, associated promotion codes and pricing, start and end dates, holiday shipping cutoffs to respect and results (spend, installs, previews, orders, ROAS, CAC). Managed by Campaign and Seasonal Promotion Management (camp) and measured by App Store Optimisation and Marketing Attribution (attr). Campaign plans contain no customer data but decide which customers are targeted through the CRM platform.
assets.businessMeaning: The plan behind blended CAC and the Q4 revenue curve: campaigns are how PastBook acquires 80% of its customers in the US against euro-based costs.
assets.accessScope: growth marketers author and run; the brand content team for creatives and translations; finance for budget; leadership for results dashboards; not visible to partners

interfaces.name: campaign api
interfaces.description: Create and schedule campaigns with channels, countries, languages, budget, creatives, promotions and cutoffs, read status and results and export the marketing calendar; used by the growth console, promotions, lifecycle messaging, attribution and localisation.

interfaces.name: campaign events
interfaces.description: Campaign scheduled, launched, budget changed, paused and ended events consumed by promotions, lifecycle messaging, attribution and analytics.

governance.retention: kept 5 years for year-over-year planning; creatives archived
governance.residency: eu; marketing platform SaaS regions per vendor agreement
governance.sharingPolicy: campaign settings shared with ad platforms and the marketing SaaS as needed to run them; results internal to PastBook

assets.name: Attribution Event
assets.description: A marketing touch or conversion attributed to a channel: ad impressions and clicks, App Store and Google Play product-page views and installs reported through the mobile measurement partner, web visits with campaign parameters, install, first preview, first order and repeat order conversions with revenue, deferred deep links from the Year in Review landing pages, the attribution model and window applied, App Tracking Transparency and consent status, and the resulting CAC and ROAS per campaign, country and channel. Collected by App Store Optimisation and Marketing Attribution (attr) through the MMP and ad platform APIs and joined with product events by Analytics and Experimentation (anly). Identifiers are hashed or pseudonymous device and attribution ids, never names.
assets.businessMeaning: The scoreboard for every marketing dollar: without trustworthy attribution the blended CAC north star and return on ad spend are guesses.
assets.accessScope: growth marketers and the platform and data team in aggregated dashboards; raw events accessible to the platform team for pipeline diagnostics; never joined to names or photos

interfaces.name: attribution api
interfaces.description: Ingest MMP and ad platform events, resolve attribution for installs and orders, read CAC and ROAS per campaign, country and channel and export conversion postbacks as consented; used by the growth console, campaigns and analytics.

interfaces.name: attribution events
interfaces.description: Install attributed, order attributed and postback sent events consumed by campaigns, lifecycle messaging and analytics.

governance.retention: raw events kept 13 months, aggregated results 5 years; events of users who opted out of tracking are never collected
